clue.text: Polishes up the East Kent regiment

definitions.meaning: to buff is to rub a surface until it shines
the old nickname, later official name, of the Royal East Kent Regiment, from its buff facings

explanation.surface: Soldiers of a Kentish regiment spruce themselves up for parade.
explanation.walkthrough: The Buffs was a British Army regiment from East Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Shines and burnishes are synonyms, and the regiment took its name from the pale leather colour of its uniform facings.

clue.text: Do they sweeten water for sailors from Avon city?

parts.note: Bath is the spa city in the old county of Avon, on the river Avon
salts, as in old salts, are experienced seamen

explanation.surface: A question about whether sailors from a West Country city improve the drinking water.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a Roman spa city in south-west England; 'sweeten' here means perfume or soften bathwater, not add sugar to drinking water.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystals tipped into a tub to scent and soften it are bath salts; the definition is a question describing them.

clue.text: Sample of what is to come from forest tea plantation

definitions.text: Sample of what is to come

indicators.note: a plantation is a planting out, so the letters of the two words are set out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A tea estate in the woods offers a first taste of its coming harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plantation' looks like part of the tea picture but tells you to rearrange FOREST and TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A preview or anticipation of later experience is a small early taste of it.

clue.text: Its aim is to retail a criminal's doings to the police

definitions.text: Its aim is to retail a criminal's doings to the police

parts.words: Its aim is to retail a criminal's doings to the police
parts.note: two readings run together: a store whose purpose is retail trade, and the slang verb for informing on a crook, since 'retail' can also mean recount or tell

explanation.surface: An informer's purpose is to pass on what a crook has been up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retail' has a second sense, to tell in detail, so the clue describes both a store and the British slang verb meaning to inform on someone to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A store exists to sell goods, and in British slang informing on a wrongdoer to the authorities is grassing or betraying them in the same word.

clue.text: Depressed, the great tsar is seen waving from a departing ship

definitions.text: seen waving from a departing ship

parts.note: Peter the Great was the tsar of Russia who founded St Petersburg

explanation.surface: A gloomy Russian emperor is spotted waving goodbye from a ship as it leaves port.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blue Peter is the blue-and-white signal flag hoisted when a ship is about to sail, so it is 'seen waving' as she departs; the tsar is not waving at all.
explanation.definitionFit: This blue flag with a white square is the naval signal that a vessel is about to put to sea.

clue.text: It is for putting up walls of a timber clad residence

definitions.meaning: lodgings that put up paying guests

definitions.text: walls of a timber clad residence
definitions.meaning: boarding is timber cladding, so a house walled in boards is literally a ...

explanation.surface: A description of a wooden-walled home and what it is built for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting up' means accommodating guests, not building, though the second half invites the building reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A guesthouse lets rooms to lodgers, and planks nailed over walls are called boarding, so the phrase also describes a plank-clad dwelling.

clue.text: Few uttered an explanation of surprise

indicators.note: uttered means the word few is spoken, and a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: the word itself, said out loud

explanation.surface: Hardly anyone could explain why they were surprised.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is a gasp of relief or astonishment, an exclamation in its own right.

clue.text: Dad's Army gets a letter giving the angle

definitions.meaning: jocularly, ... (Territorial Army), the part-time volunteer reserve of older men, written with its article
the Greek letter conventionally used in geometry to stand for an angle

explanation.surface: Veteran soldiers receive a letter explaining a particular point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army was a British sitcom about the wartime Home Guard; here it stands for the TA, Britain's Territorial Army reserve, so THE TA runs together.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth Greek letter is the usual symbol for an unknown angle in trigonometry.

clue.text: Swept up and swept back

definitions.meaning: gathered leaves or debris with a garden tool
set at a slant, as a ship's masts or a stage are sloped

explanation.surface: Something was gathered with a broom and then pushed back again.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden tool collects leaves, and an inclined mast or aircraft wing is said to have that same slant.

clue.text: Gnarled roots and trunk

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted and knotted, so the letters of roots are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: An old tree has knotted roots and a stout trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree picture makes 'trunk' look botanical; it is the human body without head and limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body, from neck to hips, is its central section.

clue.text: Where to get the best view when visiting Peveril castle

definitions.text: Where to get the best view when visiting Peveril castle

parts.words: Where to get the best view when visiting Peveril castle
parts.note: the top of a hill gives the best view, and Peveril Castle stands in the Peak District, as in Scott's novel Peveril of the Peak

explanation.surface: Advice to a tourist on the best vantage point at a Derbyshire castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Peveril Castle is a Norman ruin at Castleton in Derbyshire's Peak District, made famous by Walter Scott's novel Peveril of the Peak.
explanation.definitionFit: The summit of a hill gives the widest outlook, and this castle is linked by name with the Peak.

clue.text: A gentle heat stroke?

parts.note: a stroke can be a caress, so a soft stroke of heat is a mild dose of sunstroke

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a mild bout of sunstroke counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stroke' reads as the medical condition but also means a light touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild sunburn or slight sunstroke is described as a little contact with the solar rays.

clue.text: In the Home Counties it is sought by a developer of 13

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside another here

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A property developer hunts for something in the commuter belt around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London; the clue's 13 is the answer at 13-across, LAND, so a land developer is after a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot or building lot is what a property developer looks for before building.

clue.text: Sum a theologian has raised

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
raised means up, as in lifted

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar has brought up a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: To total figures is to calculate their sum.

clue.text: Come down to earth

definitions.meaning: to alight or touch down, as an aircraft does
ground or soil

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop daydreaming and be realistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come down to earth' is an idiom for being realistic, but it splits into two definitions joined by 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft touching down alights, and the ground itself is terra firma, both called by the same word.

clue.text: Bounder takes French man to quarters where there is a…

parts.note: a hare bounds along, so it is a bounder
M is short for Monsieur, a French man's title

explanation.surface: A cad takes a Frenchman to his lodgings, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like a cad but is literally a leaping animal. The clue runs on into 15-down: quarters where there is a curt instruction to bar men.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's quarters of a Muslim household are its seraglio, rooms where outsiders are barred.

clue.text: … curt instruction to bar men

definitions.meaning: short and to the point
a solicitor's instructions to a barrister, members of the Bar

explanation.surface: Continuing 14: a terse order keeping men out of the women's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar men' reads as excluding men but means barristers, members of the Bar, who receive written instructions from solicitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Short means concise, and a barrister's case papers are the legal term for his instructions.

clue.text: Furnish a cent somehow to an old copper-bottomed pal

annotationWithheld.why: Furnish a cent somehow to an old copper-bottomed pal: anagram of FURNISH A CENT plus D (old copper) gives the letters, but 'copper' must then also sit in the definition 'copper-bottomed pal', one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Furnish a cent somehow to an old copper-bottomed pal

clue.text: Dolly is a romantically susceptible girl

definitions.meaning: in cricket a dolly is a simple catch that should never be dropped
someone easily won over in love

explanation.surface: Dolly is described as a girl who falls in love readily.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the English bat-and-ball game, a 'dolly' is a gentle catch straight to a fielder; the girl's name is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift of a chance to dismiss a batsman, and a person readily won as a partner, share the phrase.

clue.text: Last month's speaker has room for improvement

parts.note: December is the final month of the year, abbreviated DEC
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: A speaker from December admits there is scope to do better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room for improvement' sounds like a criticism, but it means a room being smartened up by a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter and paperhanger takes a room and makes it look better.

clue.text: They arrange fresh cine sets

indicators.note: arrange tells you to put the letters of the following words into a new order

explanation.surface: Stagehands set out new scenery for filming.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer and the anagram: 'arrange' reworks FRESH CINE SETS, and stagehands who move scenery do arrange sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagehands who move scenery between acts are the people who set out and change the backdrops.

clue.text: Plagiarise work submitted by a journalist

definitions.meaning: to pass off another's work as your own, to crib
the text a reporter files for publication

explanation.surface: A reporter files an article lifted from someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbing reproduces another's writing, and reporters' filed text is called by the same newsroom word.

clue.text: Put in the box for having spied out a burglary

definitions.meaning: enclosed in a container or casing
criminal slang for reconnoitring a target before a burglary

explanation.surface: Someone was boxed up for having scouted a property before a break-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in the box' suggests a witness box or prison, but it means packed into a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Packed into a container, and, in thieves' slang, a house reconnoitred before a robbery, share the past participle.

clue.text: Provost loses street terrorist

indicators.note: loses means letters are taken away from the word before

explanation.surface: A college head has lost a road and turned to violence.
explanation.walkthrough: A Provost is the head of some colleges or a Scottish mayor; a Provo was a member of the Provisional IRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Provisional IRA, a paramilitary group, was called by this short name.

clue.text: Anything but nothing

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for anything at all
a variant of nought, zero

explanation.surface: A paradox: something that is everything except nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' looks like an exception but is just the link between two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The old word means anything whatever, and as a variant of naught it also means a zero.

clue.text: Reminder of a car's crash?

indicators.note: a crash smashes the letters of the word car's into a new order

parts.note: the word car with its s

explanation.surface: Wondering if a mark is a souvenir of a car accident.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as a picture: a mark on the skin left by a car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A healed wound leaves a lasting mark that recalls the injury.

clue.text: Only mother in France

definitions.meaning: nothing more than
the French word for mother

explanation.surface: An only parent living in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means nothing more than, and French speakers say it for mum.

clue.text: City included in the India grand tour

indicators.note: included in means the letters run inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A city that features on a grand tour of India.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters spans the end of 'India' and the start of 'grand'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taj Mahal stands in this city in Uttar Pradesh, northern India.

clue.text: Sort of fuel recommended to those who are perpetually fagged

definitions.meaning: fuel that burns without producing soot, as required in clean-air zones

definitions.text: recommended to those who are perpetually fagged
definitions.meaning: advice to chain-smokers, 'fag' being British slang for a cigarette: cut down

explanation.surface: Clean-burning coal is advised for people who are constantly worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fagged' reads as exhausted but here means always having a fag, British slang for a cigarette; such people are told to cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke and anthracite are fuels that burn cleanly, and heavy cigarette users are urged to cut down.

clue.text: Acquire sex appeal. See what I mean?

definitions.meaning: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl', so this is to gain some
a question asking whether the listener understands

explanation.surface: Someone becomes attractive, then asks if you follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtaining allure is gaining 'It', and asking whether a joke has landed is asking if someone understands.

clue.text: Get bath salts and sponge dishonestly

definitions.meaning: bath salts are the answer to 1 down, so getting them is solving clue one down
to cheat or swindle someone, sponging on them

explanation.surface: Buying toiletries and cleaning up by fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a crossword joke: the bath salts are the solution at 1-down, and to do a clue is to solve it. The phrase also means to cheat someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Solving the clue numbered one-down, and getting the better of someone by trickery, share the phrase.

clue.text: A rush to return to an ancient Assyrian city

indicators.note: to return here is to turn back over, so the letters of the two words are turned into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A dash back to an old Mesopotamian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' suggests a straight reversal, but A RUSH backwards is HSURA; the letters are turned about into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: The first capital of Assyria stood on the Tigris in what is now northern Iraq.
